newsitem.title: GERMANY: Alcatel SEL to sell German plants.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel SEL to sell German plants.

text.p: Alcatel SEL, German unit of France's Alcatel Alsthom SA, said it plans to sell a plant in Landshut that employs 608 workers and another in Stuttgart that employs 53.
The embattled electronics and engineering company said the moves will help it reduce its workforce to 13,700 by year-end from 16,000 at the end of 1996, faster than originally planned.
The company had previously said it planned to cut 1,500 jobs this year.

Alcatel SEL chairman Roland Mecklinger told journalists late on Monday that the company sees 1996 sales up six to seven percent to about 4.8 billion marks ($2.8 billion), and that it expects sales this year to exceed five billion marks.

The company still expects to post an operating loss for 1996, but to show a positive operating result this year following several years of losses, Mecklinger said. The 1996 net result will still be burdened by restructuring costs.
The Landshut plant makes electric motors and ventilation equipment, while the Stuttgart plant makes control equipment. ($ = 1.707 German Marks)
"We have to focus ourselves, and spin off activities that are not part of our core business," Mecklinger said. "We must equip ourselves with global structures."
He declined to name the prospective buyers for the two plants, or to say whether Alcatel would retain a minority stake in them.
He also said he does not see other potential spin-offs at the moment.
Alcatel SEL workers planned to protest on Tuesday against the planned job cuts.
The company will hold its annual news conference on March 18. Its operating loss in 1995 was 324 million marks.
